name: Can you keep the pool deck and remove only the pool shell?

mainEntity.name: Can the pool shell be removed while keeping the surrounding deck, patio, or coping?
mainEntity.text: Can the pool shell be removed while keeping the surrounding deck, patio, or coping?

acceptedAnswer.text: Keeping the surrounding deck or patio is sometimes possible, but it is not always the best long-term solution. If the deck is in good shape and the homeowner wants to preserve hardscape, a contractor may be able to demo only the pool shell and leave the rest in place. However, if the coping, bond beam, or adjacent slab is compromised, keeping the deck can lead to cracks, uneven edges, drainage issues, or mismatched elevations after backfill. In Los Angeles-area homes, outdoor living spaces are often integrated tightly with the pool, so the decision should be made after a site inspection. Homeowners should ask whether the deck needs saw-cutting, whether the edge will be stabilized, and how the transition area will be finished. If the goal is a clean redesign, replacing the deck at the same time may create a better final result than trying to save aging concrete.
acceptedAnswer.description: In many cases, yes, but it depends on the deck condition, edge structure, access, and how the area will be reused. Keeping the deck can save money if it is stable and not tied to the pool shell in a way that creates cracking or drainage problems. A contractor should inspect the deck before promising partial demolition.
